# Receive up to a 50% bonus when you buy Marriott Bonvoy points

**Marriott Bonvoy** has brought back a mystery bonus for buying their points. With this round of the offer it looks like some members are getting a bonus of up to 50% while others like myself have an up to 40% offer for buying points. With this promotion each member can buy up to 200,000 points annually before any bonuses, this up from the standard 150,000 points.

## The up to 50% bonus:

Receive up to a 50% bonus when you buy 2,000 or more Marriott Bonvoy points. The bonus varies by member and will be revealed when you log in. This offer is valid until Sep 9, 26 . **[Click here for more details and to buy Marriott Bonvoy Points](https://www.jdoqocy.com/click-1654157-11769493)**.

With a 50% bonus you are buying points at 0.83 cents each and 0.89 cents each if you have the 40% bonus.

We value Marriott Bonvoy points at roughly 0.7 cents per point at a minimum. That being said, we always stress it is a minimum. We’ve seen examples where redeeming points provide much higher point in value and if you can get over 0.9 cents in redemption value then it can make sense to buy them.

### Buy points for even less

If you are planning on staying at any Marriott Hotels around the world be sure to check if those hotels have an individual hotel bonus points offer available. Those bonus points offers can sometimes cost less than the best member flexible rates but in most cases are the same or slightly more than the non-member flexible rate so in effect you pay a little more to get the bonus points, thus another method of buying points. The trick here though is many times that little bit extra you pay for your stay to get the extra points is WAY cheaper than buying points from Marriott even with a 40% or higher bonus.

[**You can find the latest individual Marriott property stay bonuses on our Marriott page**](https://www.frequentflyerbonuses.com/marriott.html#count)

# Air Canada Aeroplan: Earn up to 3.5x points on select flights worldwide including Boston, Frankfurt, Manila & more (New bonuses added on July 29)

Air Canada has released a new batch of Aeroplan bonus points offers for travelling on a selection of the airline’s routes in economy and business class for the most of 2026! With this latest set of offer you need to book by August 3rd for the majority of them to earn the bonuses.

### !! A note about Aeroplan’s bonus multiplier !!

Just a note that Air Canada applies a different style of math when it comes to their flight bonus multipliers.

For example, typically when a bonus offer is advertised as 2x points it is double your base earning amount, such as 1,000 points becomes 2,000 points. However, Air Canada Aeroplan is now taking the multiplied amount and adding it on top of base points. That is,  if you earn 1,000 base points, and the bonus offer is 2x, they will take the 2x points which would be 2,000 points and add it to the base earn where you would end up earning 3,000 points. Basically it works out to 3x points in the context of all other bonus offers we have published on FFB for 20+ years.

I dug into this after seeing a 1x points offer and thought to myself, why would they be advertising that as a bonus if you aren’t multiplying your base amount? Well it turns out that 1x points is actually 2x points as their example of 500 points means you’ll earn a total of 1,000 points.

I hope that helps everyone make sense of Air Canada’s bonus multipliers!

# Hyatt Globalist Status: How To Earn It and What Perks You’ll Get

Hyatt Globalist status isn’t just another top-tier hotel loyalty level — it’s one of the most coveted elite statuses in the travel world. Hyatt Globalist benefits include free suite upgrades, waived resort fees, free breakfast, and even access to a dedicated concierge.

But earning Hyatt Globalist status takes real strategy, whether you're racking up nights, earning base points, or combining your hotel stays with smart credit card spending. Here’s everything you need to know about earning World of Hyatt Globalist and Lifetime Globalist status, the benefits you'll enjoy, and whether it’s worth pursuing.

## How To Get Hyatt Globalist Status

Hyatt Globalist elite status requires travelers to hit one of two metrics to earn this top-tier status:

* Stay 60 nights
* Earn 100,000 base points

Thankfully you don't have to actually sleep 60 nights in a Hyatt hotel to earn Hyatt Globalist. There are a few shortcuts we'll cover below.

[图片：lounge chairs around a pool with the Hyatt logo on the hotel tower]*Grand Hyatt Muscat. Credit: Hyatt*

**Related: [The World of Hyatt Program — A Complete Guide](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/world-of-hyatt/)**

### Staying at Hyatt Hotels

The most straightforward way to earn Globalist status with Hyatt is by spending nights in a Hyatt property. You can [earn Hyatt qualifying nights](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/world-of-hyatt/elite-night-credits/) from both paid stays as well as award redemptions.

Note that reservations booked through third-party platforms — like Expedia, Hotels.com, or even some Chase Travel portal reservations — are ineligible to earn qualifying nights within the [World of Hyatt program](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/world-of-hyatt/), so they should be avoided if the end goal is earning status or enjoying the perks once you have earned it.

### Earning base points

If 60 nights seems insurmountable, you can alternatively reach World of Hyatt Globalist by earning 100,000 base points each year. World of Hyatt members generally earn 5X base points for each dollar they spend on eligible hotel charges, including room rates, dining, spa services, and other eligible purchases at participating Hyatt hotels and resorts.

Hyatt Studios is an exception, with stays earning 2.5X base points per dollar spent.

Back-of-the-napkin math means that at the standard 5X earning rate, you'd need to spend $20,000 a year at Hyatt to earn and keep Globalist status.

Additionally, you can rack up base points toward top-tier Hyatt status through the following:

* 5X base points per dollar spent on stays at Homes & Hideaways by World of Hyatt.
* 10X base points per dollar spent on FIND experiences.

Just keep in mind that only base points count toward Globalist status; bonus points don't.

[图片：Aerial view of Secrets Tulum Resort & Spa]*Secrets Tulum Resort & Spa. Credit: Hyatt*

### Spending on your Hyatt credit cards

If you hold either the personal or business version of the World of Hyatt credit card, you can use it to spend your way to Hyatt Globalist.

[The World of Hyatt Credit Card](https://awardwallet.com/credit-cards/world-of-hyatt/chase-hyatt-card/) awards **five qualifying night credits annually** plus **two additional qualifying night credits for every $5,000** spent on the card.

But you'll also earn more than just an accelerated path to Hyatt status. You'll earn Hyatt points when you spend on the card — with bonus points on everything from hotel stays to local transit, commuting, and gym memberships.

You'll receive a [Category 1–4 free night certificate](https://awardwallet.com/hotels/world-of-hyatt/hyatt-category-4/) each year you have this credit card, and you can earn another free night certificate after spending $15,000 on purchases annually. These free night certificates are valid at any properties in Category 1–4, and a Hyatt member can redeem a free night for a one-night stay or as part of a longer stay. You'll also earn elite-qualifying night credits on eligible award stays booked with Hyatt points or free night awards.

World of Hyatt Globalist members can enjoy complimentary space-available upgrades at check-in — including standard suites. Premium suites, however, remain out of reach to Globalists unless a specific property decides to upgrade as a courtesy.

Some properties don't participate in these upgrades at all, such as Hyatt Vacation Club or Hyatt House, but you should still be able to enjoy these upgrades on your next stays at the majority of Hyatt's brands, including its premium Park Hyatt properties.

**1. Preferential Seating**

This wasn’t identified on the boarding pass, and I couldn’t tell whether there was even one when you enter the secure area.

The boarding pass correctly displayed my MileagePlus status (Gold), but the self service lounge entry gave an error and prompted me to check with the desk.

# Elite status via the Air France KLM credit card

I’m intrigued by the possibility of earning Air France KLM Flying Blue Platinum elite status. Two features of Platinum status are particularly compelling to me: 1) better access to lowest-level awards (such as 60K for business class between the U.S. and Europe); and 2) the ability to change and cancel awards for free. To decide whether it’s worth pursuing, I first had to wrap my head around how Flying Blue elite status works and how the [Air France KLM Visa Signature® Credit Card](https://frequentmiler.com/afklm/) can help. This post is intended to be a general primer on the topic, and it should be useful too for those interested in earning Silver or Gold status (either of which can be useful when flying Delta).

## Flying Blue Elite Status

Before detailing how the Air France KLM credit card can help, let’s cover Flying Blue elite status, in general…

### Elite Status Requirements

Flying Blue elite status is achieved by earning XP (Experience Points). Silver requires 100 XP, Gold requires 180 XP, and Platinum requires 300 XP. Unlike programs that have fixed elite-earning years (usually calendar year), Flying Blue status is based on XPs earned in the 12 months since you last achieved a level of status. For example, once you move from no status (Explorer) to Silver, you have 12 months to earn enough XP to maintain Silver status (100 XP) or move up to Gold (180 XP). Here are the XPs required to earn or maintain each status level:

* Silver Status: 100 XP
* Gold Status: 180 XP
* Platinum Status: 300 XP
* Ultimate Status: 900 UXP. UXP = XP earned from flying Air France or KLM. Since this is an extremely high bar, and since UXP can’t be earned from the credit card, I’ll no longer discuss Ultimate Status in this post.

Note that you can’t jump directly from no status to Gold with 180 XP or to Platinum with 300 XP. Instead, you need to earn Silver status first, then earn 180 XP to get to Gold, then earn 300 XP to get to Platinum. Once you’re at a particular level, though, you can maintain status with 100 XP for Silver, 180 XP for Gold, or 300 XP for Platinum.

### Elite Status Benefits

| **Delta Sky Club access** | | You + 1 Guest\* |

\* *Sky Club access is available only when flying on the same day on an **international SkyTeam flight**, or on a domestic flight connecting to an international flight.*

### XP Rollover

When you reach a new status level, or maintain an existing one, the XPs required for that level are deducted from your account, but any extras remain. For example, let’s say that you had Silver status and then earned 200 XP. 180 XP would be deducted from your account in order to grant you Gold status, and 20 XP would remain. So you’d have 20 XP toward maintaining Gold status or toward earning Platinum status. Rollovers are capped at 300 XP.

### Soft Landings

Flying Blue will never drop you more than one elite level per year. For example, if you earn Platinum status but don’t earn any XP over the next 12 months, you’ll be dropped to Gold.

### Credit Card Elite Earning

The Air France KLM Visa Signature® Credit Card offers multiple ways to earn XPs:

* Welcome bonus: **100 XP**
* Account anniversary: **20 XP**
* Earn up to **140 XP** through spend (awarded on your account anniversary):

 + Earn an additional 60 XP each anniversary after $25,000 in qualifying purchases within the anniversary year

### Using the card to earn and maintain Silver status

The Air France KLM card makes it super easy to maintain Silver status. For flying Delta, that means getting a free checked bag and preferred seat selection.

Since Silver status requires only 100 XP, this card’s welcome bonus alone will get you there. Then, I believe that you can maintain Silver status as follows:

* Year 1:
 + Sign up for the card and meet its minimum spend requirements. Earn **100 XP** from the welcome bonus. You will then get Silver status, and those 100 XP will be deducted from your account.
 + Spend $15,000 during your first membership year and earn **100 XP** on your cardmember anniversary (20 XP is automatic + 80 XP from spend). Silver status will renew 12 months from when it was granted and 100 XP will be subtracted from your account.
* Future years: Spend $15,000 and earn 100 XP each cardmember anniversary.

**Short version**: To earn and maintain Silver status, simply spend $15,000 each year on the card.

### Using the card to earn and maintain Gold status

Gold status (which requires 180 XP) adds Delta Sky Club access, but only on international itineraries. If that interests you, here’s a path:

* Year 1:
 + Sign up for the card, but don’t yet meet its minimum spend requirements.
 + Find a way to get temporary status ([through a status match, for example](https://frequentmiler.com/flying-blue-status-match-for-us-residents/)) before earning the welcome bonus. This is important because if you don’t have status, the welcome bonus 100 XP will be “wasted” by earning Silver status.
 + Earn **100 XP** from the welcome bonus.
 + Spend $25,000 during your first membership year and earn **160 XP** on your cardmember anniversary (20 XP is automatic + 140 XP from spend). You should now have 260 XP.
 + 12 months from your temporary status, 180 of your 260 XP will be deducted in order to grant you another year of Gold status. **80 XP should roll over**.
* Year 2:
 + Spend $25,000 and earn **160 XP** on your next cardmember anniversary. Thanks to the 80 XP rollover, you should now have 240 XP.
 + 180 of your 240 XP will be deducted in order to grant you another year of Gold status. **60 XP should roll over**.
* Year 3:
 + Spend $25,000 and earn **160 XP** on your next cardmember anniversary. Thanks to the 60 XP rollover, you should now have 220 XP.
 + 180 of your 220 XP will be deducted in order to grant you another year of Gold status. **40 XP should roll over**.

**Short version**: If you time things right by first signing up for the Air France KLM card, then obtaining a status match, and then meeting the minimum spend, you should be able to earn and maintain Gold status for many years simply by spending $25,000 per year on the card.

### Using the card to earn and maintain Platinum status

Platinum status (which requires 300 XP) is where the gold is. You need this status to unlock better Air France KLM lowest-award-fare availability, free award changes and cancellations, and the ability to book La Première first-class awards. Unfortunately, it’s also a stretch to maintain long-term, even with the Air France KLM card.

* Year 1:
 + Sign up for the card, but don’t yet meet its minimum spend requirements.
 + Find a way to get temporary **Gold** status ([through a status match, for example](https://frequentmiler.com/flying-blue-status-match-for-us-residents/)) before earning the welcome bonus. This is important because if you don’t have Gold status, the welcome bonus 100 XP will be “wasted” by earning Silver or Gold status. If you already have status before getting the card, things get even more complicated.
 + Earn **100 XP** from the welcome bonus.
 + Spend $25,000 during your first membership year and earn **160 XP** on your cardmember anniversary (20 XP is automatic + 140 XP from spend). You should now have **260 XP**.
 + Earn 40 XP through flying and other means. Worst case: donate 80,000 Flying Blue miles to earn **40 XP.**
 + Once you earn Platinum status, all 300 XP will be deducted.
* Years 2 and beyond (this is where it gets hard!)
 + Earn a total of 160 XP through card spend
 + Earn 140 XP through other means. [This SkyStatus post](https://skystatus.pro/guide/flying-blue-earn-xp-fast) details many tricks for earning XP quickly and easily.

## Conclusion

Flying Blue elite status is obviously useful for those who fly Air France or KLM regularly. For the rest of us, there are some reasons to pursue status. For example, if you fly Delta occasionally, Flying Blue elite status offers free preferred seat selection and a free checked bag. The Air France KLM credit card makes it easy to earn and keep Silver status with $15,000 spent per year, or Gold status with $25,000 spent per year. Platinum status is even more attractive, but it can’t be achieved with the credit card alone. Plus, it requires careful timing to maximize the credit card’s first-year XP bonus. In my case, right before losing Bilt Platinum status in January, I activated Bilt’s Flying Blue Gold status match ([details here](https://frequentmiler.com/bilt-adds-flying-blue-gold-status-match-for-platinum-members/)). So, now I have Gold status until January 2027. To maximize the Air France KLM card’s XP bonus to help me reach Platinum status, I believe I need to wait until my Gold status expires, then apply for the card, then wait a bit and activate the Gold status match again before meeting the card’s minimum spend. So, for now, I’m learning and plotting. If you have suggestions for better ways to get to Flying Blue Platinum status, please comment below.

# Airport lounge access with Accor elite status

A couple of weeks ago, on an [episode of Frequent Miler on the Air](https://frequentmiler.com/turn-hotel-status-into-airline-status-frequent-miler-on-the-air-ep367-7-17-26/), Greg and Nick talked through various ways of getting airline elite status through hotel elite status. As part of the main event, they discussed a couple of interesting status matching opportunities with All Accor, the loyalty program of Accor Hotels and Resorts.

All Accor continues to be a program that flies under the radar in the US, primarily due to the lack of a domestic footprint, no US credit cards, and less-than-1:1 transfer ratios from all major bank currencies. However, there’s a whole new wave of Accor Gold and Platinum members, by virtue of [Bilt’s August Rent Day](https://frequentmiler.com/rent-day-all-accor-status-offer-for-bilt-members-with-points-transfer/) promotion, which allowed Bilt elite members to earn Accor elite status by transferring a modest amount of Bilt points to Accor.

Given that, we thought it was the perfect time to highlight a couple of those matching opportunities with Accor, one of which can get you a year’s worth of domestic airport lounge access.

[Complete Guide to ALL Accor](https://frequentmiler.com/complete-guide-accor-loyalty-program/)

## The Deals

* Accor elite members with Gold status or higher can obtain SkyTeam Elite Plus via a status match to Kenya Air Platinum Elite Plus. (h/t: [MilesTalk](https://milestalk.com/interesting-status-match-accor-gold-to-skyteam-elite-plus/))
 + Status includes access for the member and one guest to airport lounges worldwide (except for the US), regardless of class of travel.
 + [See list of lounges here](https://a.storyblok.com/f/271050/x/e9b8411817/domestic-lounge-list-october-2025.pdf)
 + Also includes additional baggage allowance, priority boarding, and more
 + Kenya Airways charges $299 for the status match

[**Direct Link to Offer**](https://kenya-airways.statusmatch.com/?fpr=0ht6hd)

* Accor elite members with Platinum status or higher can obtain oneworld Sapphire status via a status match to Qatar Airways Gold.
 + Status includes access for the member and one guest to airport lounges worldwide, regardless of class of travel.
 + Includes access to American Airlines Admirals Clubs, business class Flagship Lounges, and Alaska Lounges with one guest
 + Qatar allows a limited number of matches per year; it’s possible that 2026 may already be full
 + You must complete one paid, Qatar-marketed and -operated flight after linking accounts in order to match status
 + **Note that oneworld Sapphire status earned through Alaska or AA does NOT give you domestic lounge access; only if it’s earned through a foreign carrier (like Qatar)**
* How to match status
 + [Link your ALL and Qatar accounts](https://www.qatarairways.com/en/Privilege-Club/our-partners/accor.html)
 + Add your Qatar Privilege Club number to an eligible Qatar reservation and take the flight
 + Officially, the upgrade will happen upon completion of the flight; in practice, your status is usually upgraded at check-in ([full terms](https://www.qatarairways.com/en/Privilege-Club/terms-and-conditions/accor-account-linking.html))

[**Direct Link to Offer**](https://www.qatarairways.com/en/Privilege-Club/our-partners/accor.html)

## Quick Thoughts

Of the two, the Kenya Airways version is less appealing, as Delta Sky Club access is excluded. However, you can get into a fairly extensive array of SkyTeam member lounges, such as Air France and SAS. You also get a free bag for you and everyone on your reservation, even on economy fares. That could be worth $299 for a family, depending on their travel patterns.

The Qatar match is obviously much more interesting, due to the ability to access domestic American and Alaska lounges. This one requires Accor Platinum status (Gold members can match to the less interesting Qatar Silver) AND you have to fly at least one paid Qatar Airways flight. However, unlike the first example with Kenya Airways, there’s no additional fee.

You can see [Qatar’s route map here](https://www.flightconnections.com/route-map-qatar-airways-qr); my assumption is that the cheapest options would be short-haul flights around the Middle East, but Qatar also operates several [fifth-freedom flights](https://www.australianfrequentflyer.com.au/fifth-freedom-routes/#h-our-list-of-fifth-freedom-routes) (that don’t begin or end in Qatar), including from Ho Chi Minh City to Phnom Penh and from Brisbane (soon Melbourne) and Auckland.

The Accor to Qatar match has a strange quirk. The [terms that Qatar publishes](https://www.qatarairways.com/en/Privilege-Club/terms-and-conditions/accor-account-linking.html) cap the total number of Gold matches at 3,100 for 2026. I haven’t found any good information on whether that cap has been reached; some Qatar agents have told customers that it’s dead for the year, but there are [recent examples](https://www.flyertalk.com/forum/accor-all-accor-live-limitless/2095715-accor-qatar-partnership-24.html?styleid=24) of folks still receiving upgraded status. If you’re interested in the match but don’t need to fly Qatar this year, it might be best to wait ’til 2027, when a fresh quota will likely be launched.

[The best credit cards for Priority Pass Lounges](https://frequentmiler.com/best-priority-pass-cards/)

As for me, neither of these potential matches moves the needle. Because of my credit cards, I get access to so many lounges, including Priority Pass, Centurion and Sapphire. I have regular day passes to Alaska and AA lounges, and when I fly international business class, lounges are part of the deal. I can’t remember the last time I was in an airport, wanted to get into a lounge, and didn’t have at least one option.

That said, these are still fun options to know about, and I’m sure that there are at least a few folks out there who can get great value from them.

 + Book & fly 2 round trip flights (or 4 qualifying one way flights) & earn promotional A-List status that’s valid through December 31, 2026

* Rapid Rewards Members (“Member”) can earn promotional A-List status valid through 12/31/2026 and Rapid Rewards bonus points when registering, booking in Eligible Distribution Channels, and flying qualifying flights for this Promotion between 7/28/2026 and 10/31/2026 (the “Promotion Period”).
* During the Promotion Period, Member must register for this Promotion by completing the Promotion’s registration form and then, subject to the Rapid Rewards restrictions set forth below, Member can: (i) earn promotional A-List status (valid through 12/31/2026) after booking and flying two (2) qualifying round trip flights (or four (4) qualifying one-way flights), and (ii) also earn 20,000 Rapid Rewards bonus points after booking and flying four (4) qualifying round trip flights (or eight (8) qualifying one-way flights), provided that such **qualifying flights are booked through swabiz.com (SWABIZ®), Global Distribution System (GDS), or one of our direct connect/API partners through Southwest Partner Services (SPS) distribution channels with Southwest Airlines inventory** (each, an “Eligible Distribution Channel”) and each booking includes Member’s Rapid Rewards account number at the time of booking.

* Offer valid on new reservations booked and flown within the Promotion Period only.
* A qualifying round trip flight is a round trip flight on Southwest Airlines from an origin city to a destination city and back to the originating airport or carrier-recognized co-terminal, and a qualifying one-way flight is a one-way flight on Southwest Airlines from an origin city to a destination city.
* For purposes of this Promotion, a qualifying flight must be a flight operated by Southwest Airlines and paid with dollars, Southwest LUV Vouchers, gift cards, or flight credits, and those paid with Cash + Points.
* **Qualifying flights exclude reward flights**, charter flights, nonrevenue travel, Getaways by Southwest vacation bookings, **and Companion Pass travel**.
* Travel booked or flown prior to Member’s registration for this Promotion is not considered a qualifying flight for this Promotion.
* Rapid Rewards bonus points earned through this Promotion are in addition to the regular Rapid Rewards points earned through Rapid Rewards.
* Changes made to the itinerary after purchase may eliminate qualification for this Promotion.
* This Promotion cannot be combined with any other promotional offer.

* Current A-List status Members whose status is expiring during the Promotion Period are eligible to earn promotional A-List status under this Promotion, and the promotional A-List status earned under this Promotion will supersede and replace Member’s existing A-List status if such status has not yet expired.
* If Member qualifies for promotional A-List status during the Promotion Period, then Member will not receive an A-List card, but Member will receive all A-List status benefits on all flights booked after being awarded promotional A-List status, when Member provides their Rewards account number when making their reservation.
* If regular A-List status is earned by Member by flying 20 qualifying one-way flights or earning 35,000 tier qualifying points in the 2026 calendar year while qualified for promotional A-List status, the regular A-List status will supersede the promotional A-List status, entitling the Member to A-List status through December 31, 2027.

## Quick Thoughts

Southwest A-List status usually requires taking 20 one way flights or by earning 35,000 tier qualifying points. This promotion slashes the flight requirement by 80% seeing as you only need to take 4 one way (or 2 round trip) flights in order to get A-List status. That makes it much easier to achieve, although do note that the status earned via this promotion expires at the end of 2026, whereas A-List status earned in the conventional way would be valid through the end of 2027.

If you take 8 one way flights (or 4 round trips), you’ll get an additional 20,000 bonus Rapid Rewards points. It’s unlikely that that’ll make it worth a mileage run unless you only need one (or maybe two) further one way flights after the rest of your travel, but it’s a very good reward nonetheless.

Something important to be aware of is that the flights have to be booked via SWABIZ, GDS, or another qualifying partner that can book business flights. Ultimately, it doesn’t matter if you’re *actually* flying for business, plus my understanding is that SWABIZ fares match those you’ll find on Southwest.com, so it’s not like you’re being forced to pay a higher fare in order to take advantage of this promotion.

Nick reminded me that if you’re not currently registered for SWABIZ, it’s worth having your partner (if you have one) refer you. That’s because [if you refer someone for SWABIZ](https://business.southwest.com/referacompany) and they register and complete 1 round trip or 2 one way flights within 90 days, the person referring the business gets 25,000 bonus Rapid Rewards points.

Also be aware that flights booked entirely with Rapid Rewards points aren’t eligible, nor are flights where a Companion Pass is being used *if you’re the companion*. If you’re the person with a Companion Pass and you’re traveling with your Companion, you’ll still be eligible if you’ve paid a cash fare or a fare with Cash + Points. You also have to register before booking qualifying flights and those flights have to be completed by October 31, 2026. Even if you have flights booked via SWABIZ that’ll take place during the promotion period, those won’t count if they were booked before registering for this promo.

This is likely a targeted promotion. When trying to register for it, you’ll need to be logged in to your Rapid Rewards account. After logging in and visiting the registration page, you should see a yellow ‘Register Now’ button. If you do, you’re targeted. If you don’t see that button, that unfortunately means you’re not eligible for this offer.

Depending on any elite status you currently hold with other airlines and your upcoming travel plans, it might make sense to utilize [Southwest’s status match feature](https://www.southwest.com/rapid-rewards/promotions/status-match/) instead. Even if you have low level status with other domestic airlines, you can match to A-List status for 120 days and extend that for an additional 12 months if, during those 120 days, you fly 3 round trips or 6 one way flights. Those are slightly higher requirements than this limited time promotion, but the status match avenue gives you 120 days to complete the requirements—more than the ~90 days from this offer. Status matching doesn’t award 20,000 bonus points though.

That said, I did stay at an NH Collection hotel in Brussels a couple of years ago (booked through Amex Fine Hotels & Resorts to use a prepaid hotel credit), and we were very happy with our stay (I didn’t write a full review, but [it got a mention in this post](https://frequentmiler.com/belgium-beer-beauty-castles-chocolate-and-fhr-and-fnc-success/)). I’ve noticed that a number of NH Collection properties have appeared in my recent searches through Fine Hotels & Resorts and/or Chase’s The Edit. Those searches have almost all been for overseas hotels; the GHA Discovery footprint is far smaller in the US than overseas.

While [full status benefits can be found here](https://www.ghadiscovery.com/gha-discovery-benefits), key benefits at the top two status tiers include:

* **GHA Platinum**: 6% back in Discovery Dollars (hotel rewards), Welcome Amenity, 3 pm late checkout (subject to availability), and room upgrade (subject to availability)
* **GHA Titanium**: 7% back in Discovery Dollars (hotel rewards), Welcome Amenity, Complimentary Breakfast at some brands, Double upgrade (based on availability), 11 am check-in (based on availability), 4 pm late checkout (based on availability), Status Sharing (sounds similar to Hyatt’s Guest of Honor, though **note that this benefit is not available to those matching**, so you won’t be able to share your matched status unless you requalify), and more

The benefits at top-tier Titanium are obviously far more compelling. Since they are matching easy-to-get hotel statuses like IHG Platinum (which is now a benefit for new Chase Sapphire Reserve cardholders and also comes as a benefit of the IHG Rewards Premier and IHG Rewards Business credit cards) and Hilton Honors Diamond (which comes as a standard benefit on the Hilton Honors Aspire card), I imagine that many readers will qualify for a match to Titanium (those with harder-to-get Hyatt Globalist and Marriott Platinum or higher also match to GHA Discovery Titanium).

Unfortunately, many of the GHA Discovery Titanium benefits are based on availability, and I imagine that recognition of those benefits varies widely by brand and even by location. I far prefer guaranteed benefits to those that might be available to me even without status. That said, with SLH and Greg’s experiences with Preferred Hotels having increased my interest in boutique hotels in recent years, I could imagine the benefits working out well in some instances. I would particularly appreciate the early check-in upon arrival in Europe, though, again, I don’t love it being based on availability.

I wouldn’t recommend throwing down $150 on the off *chance* you *might* book a qualifying property by the end of 2027, but if you have plans that include some of their brands or destinations where they have a strong footprint, it might be worth considering. As my travel plans for next year start to come into focus, and with a number of Edit credits / potentially expanded Fine Hotels & Resorts credits on the table now or in the near future, I might consider this match.

类似于汉莎，日航会员体系升级要求定级分中有部分必须来自于本集团，而万豪赠送的定积分竟然划在此列！也就是说，钛金和大使会员每年都可以直接获得日航的水晶会籍（对应于寰宇一家**红宝石**）；而**蓝宝石**的门槛为50,000点定级分，可以通过日航或者伙伴航司补足。

# 马来西亚航空会籍匹配活动

今天说个会籍匹配活动以及延伸知识，虽然绝大多数读者可能用不上但简单了解一下吧。

主角为[马来西亚航空](https://enrich.statusmatch.com/)：

* 仅面向印度航空和印尼鹰航的会员
* 不可以是马来西亚的公民
* 对应级别可匹配至马航的银卡 / 金卡 / 白金
* 费用分别为$89 / $199 / $349
* 匹配成功后，会籍有效期为12个月

活动意义不大，首先不是免费、其次限制了两家航空公司，基本就是奔着去印度和印尼抢会员去了。之所以还是提这么一嘴是因为印尼鹰航恰好有一个卖金卡的活动！

鹰航这个特别的项目叫做[Gold Privilege](https://www.garuda-indonesia.com/my/en/garudamiles/tentang-garudamiles/goldprivilege)，入会费用是$399，之后续费只要$299（使用印尼盾支付还能再便宜些）。项目权益包括：

* **金卡**会籍（等同天合联盟**精英**）
* 五张商务舱休息室入场券
* 里程票兑换九折优惠
* 旅行保险

完全不用保级，每年只要续费交钱就可以，十分人性化的政策？这张金卡在联盟内（东航、厦航、法航荷航及达美等）可享受优先值机登机，额外托运行李额度以及选座优惠等权益。

也就是说理论上你支付不到六百美元就可以收获一张天合联盟精英以及一张寰宇一家蓝宝石，但也只是说说，并不推荐你这么做——价格贵还是其次，这张买来的金卡能不能用来匹配马航还是未知数。

# 法航荷航和北欧航空会籍匹配

今天说两个会籍匹配活动，都是天合联盟。

#### 北欧航空

[北欧航空的会籍匹配](https://sas.statusmatch.com/)又回来了，可惜和绝大多数读者无缘：

* 仅限印度居民
* 支持印度航空、英国航空、汉莎航空、阿联酋航空、卡塔尔航空、土耳其航空和美联航
* 可匹配至银卡、金卡或者钻卡
* 费用为€39 / €79 / €159

可以说是物美价廉，可惜这个居住地要求，当然不信邪的话你也可以改个IP看能不能蒙混过关（估计很难）。话说针对印度市场推出这个活动很奇怪，北欧航空在印度也只有孟买一个航点。

#### 法航荷航

[另一个就是大家的老朋友蓝翔了](https://flyingblue.statusmatch.com/)。他们的（付费）会籍匹配几乎是常青树，只不过匹配标准一直在变化，最近又将大中华区加了回来：

* 支持国航、南航、海航、国泰、汉莎、英航、土航等众多航司
* 银卡、金卡匹配的费用分别为$99 / $299
* 大中华区不支持白金匹配

最划算的是英国，不但可以匹配到白金而且价格最便宜。

北欧航空和蓝翔的银卡都是天合联盟**精英**，乘坐成员航班比如东方航空、厦门航空、中华航空、维珍航空和达美航空等可享受选座优惠，优先值机、登机以及额外托运行李。金卡及以上则是**超级精英**，增加快速通道和商务舱休息室等权益。
